comments.body:
Hi there! It looks like your issue requires a minimal reproducible example, but it is invalid or absent. Please prepare such an example and share it in a new issue.

  **The best way to get attention to your issue is to provide a clean and easy way for a developer to reproduce the issue on their own machine.** Please do not provide your entire project, or a project with more code than is necessary to reproduce the issue.

  A side benefit of going through the process of narrowing down the minimal amount of code needed to reproduce the issue is that you may get lucky and discover that the bug is due to a mistake in your application code that you can quickly fix on your own.

  ### Resources

  - ["How to create a Minimal, Reproducible Example"](https://stackoverflow.com/help/minimal-reproducible-example)
  - ["How to narrow down the source of an error"](https://expo.fyi/manual-debugging)

  ### Common concerns

  #### "I've only been able to reproduce it in private, proprietary code"

  You may not have spent enough time narrowing down the root cause of the issue. Try out the techniques discussed in this [manual debugging guide](https://expo.fyi/manual-debugging) to learn how to isolate the problem from the rest of your codebase.

  #### "I didn't have time to create one"

  That's understandable, it can take some time to prepare. We ask that you hold off on filing an issue until you are able to fully complete the required fields in the issue template.

  #### "You can reproduce it by yourself by creating a project and following these steps"

  This is useful knowledge, but it's still valuable to have the resulting project that is produced from running the steps, where you have verified you can reproduce the issue.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
I am currently using **Expo SDK version ~51.0.28** with **Node.js v18.20.5,** and everything works fine. 
However, when I upgrade to Expo SDK 52 or later while using Node.js 20, I encounter issues. I have successfully reproduced the problem, and it seems to be related to Node.js 20 compatibility with Expo 52+.

comments.author: participant8
comments.body:
I just resolved my issue without needing to downgrade.

The solution was to install the following packages:

- react-native-safe-area-context
- react-native-screens
- react-native-svg

Let me know if this works for you too!

comments.body:
If you're developing a project with Expo and using Firebase, and you get a blank screen when building the APK, try this:

When you build the project, make sure to include the google-services.json file in the **"android"** folder, which would normally be in the root of the project. If you don't have this folder, you can generate it with the "npx expo prebuild" command. Then, in `"android/app/"`, you'll put the **"google-services.json"** file. Then, in the **"app.json"** file (in the root of the Expo project), add this configuration:

```
"android": {
"package": "com.yourpackage.name",
"adaptiveIcon": {
"foregroundImage": "./assets/adaptive-icon.png",
"backgroundColor": "#ffffff"
},
"googleServicesFile": "./android/app/google-services.json"
},
```

And that's it, you can build the project. apk with:
`eas build --profile production --platform android`
or also:
`eas build -p android --clear-cache --profile preview`

I have solved my problem, it was actually quite stupid but I didn't notice until now.

When building my app as a preview build through EAS, it was not picking my env variables set in my `.env.local` file, while if i'm not wrong when building for production it does.
You have to manually add the env variables that you want in the EAS console for the preview environment (if you want also for the others).

A quick check to know if you env variables are loaded correctly is to look at the terminal just after you run the `eas build` command, if they are loaded correctly you can see them mentioned like in this example:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/003c68ff-5e9c-41e7-8ce6-f9d1b926e122)


Here you can find the reference for setting the enviromental variable for the different enviroment on eas: https://docs.expo.dev/eas/environment-variables/

I was having the same issue and solved it doing the following:
Built a preview version of the app (because I wasn't able to reproduce the bug in expo go) npx eas-cli build --platform ios --profile preview
Downloaded the .app file and installed it on my xcode simulator (I downloaded this from the expo build page)
Opened the native "Console" app in macOS (it's literally called Console)
Selected on the left the simulation device under the devices section
Filtered the logs for errors and faults by clicking the "Errors and defaults" button right above the datagrid and then I added another filter for process name on the searchbox with the name of my app.
Restarted the blank page app and then I checked ALL the logs for my app that were related to errors and fauls and found one that said
Invariant Violation: TurboModuleRegistry.getEnforcing(...): 'RNGestureHandlerModule' could not be found. Verify that a module by this name is registered in the native binary.
After googling this I found that what happened is that some packages are included in Expo Go but NOT in standalone builds and need to be explicitly included.
The package I was missing was participant54native-gesture-handler
after installing that package, I rebuilt my preview version of the app, ran it on my simulator and the app was working again. After that I created another production build, sent it to testflight and everything was working fine again.
Hope this helps, maybe your error is not the same but with the console you will surely find it
wrote an article about this error in case you are interested
https://medium.com/@matias.turra/participant54native-expo-app-shows-blank-screen-on-testflight-but-works-in-expo-go-de6d184ed96d
